reason: Rewrite R_{a,b,r}(q) as product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i))/(1 - q^i). Under q -> q^(-1), each factor picks up a factor q^(-r), so R_{a,b,r}(q^(-1)) = q^(-r(b-a)) R_{a,b,r}(q) = q^(-D) R_{a,b,r}(q). If R is a polynomial, this identity forces degree at most D; after padding coefficients with zeros up to D, comparing coefficients in q^D R(q^(-1)) = R(q) gives c_j = c_{D-j}.
